bull.b: SkyEMS 3.0 expands Flux Power beyond battery hardware by adding monitoring, diagnostics and fleet-uptime capabilities. Broad inclusion across GFC batteries can deepen customer integration, support differentiated performance, and create a more durable value proposition for electrified fleets.

Certification and coverage across leading OEMs strengthen Flux Power’s access to the industrial vehicle ecosystem. This channel position can support repeat adoption, improve credibility with fleet customers, and provide a foundation for broader battery sales as electrification expands.

Meaningful operating-expense reductions improve the company’s ability to scale if demand recovers, because less revenue is required to support the cost base. Continued discipline could help preserve cash and narrow losses, although profitability remains dependent on revenue improvement.

bear.b: The sharp annual revenue decline indicates weakened demand and reduced operating scale rather than a temporary quarterly fluctuation. Lower volume limits absorption of fixed costs, pressures profitability, and makes management’s expected recovery dependent on renewed customer spending.

Required equity fundraising and continued default status show that Flux Power has limited financial flexibility over the coming months. Dependence on lender discretion and potential dilution can constrain investment, complicate execution, and leave the business vulnerable if funding is delayed.

Lower gross margins reduce the contribution available to cover operating expenses and fund growth. Product mix, tariffs and lost operating leverage have already weakened profitability, so even a revenue rebound may not translate into sustainable earnings unless margins recover.
